lakshmisharath on September 1, 2026: "One sacred hill town. Three completely different temple worlds.

In Amarkantak, the Narmada begins her sacred journey, thousand-year-old Kalachuri temples take you into another era, and four enormous faces rise above the extraordinary Shri Yantra Mandir.

This is where rivers, gods and sacred geometry meet.

📍 THE QUICK GUIDE TO AMARKANTAK 🗺️👇

Revered as Teerthraj (the King of Pilgrimage Sites), this hidden hill town in Madhya Pradesh is a paradise for history, architecture, and heritage lovers.

🕌 THE SPOTS TO VISIT:• 

Maa Narmada Temple: The pristine white origin of the sacred Narmada River at Udgam Kund.

Kalachuri Temples: 1,000-year-old stone marvels held together by pure gravity, including the Pataleshwar gateway.

Shri Yantra Mandir: A jaw-dropping geometric monument sculpted as a 3D structural Shri Chakra.

🚗 HOW TO REACH:• 

🚂 Train: Pendra Road Station is the closest railhead (42 km away).• 

🚗 Road: Well-connected by scenic road routes from Bilaspur (120 km) or Jabalpur (214 km).• 

✈️ Air: Nearest domestic airports are in Jabalpur or Raipur.

📅 BEST TIME TO VISIT:• October to March for beautiful, cool weather.• July to September (Monsoon) to see the surrounding Maikal hills covered in dense green mist and flowing waterfalls.

⏱️ RECOMMENDED STAY: 1 to 2 days is the absolute sweet spot to explore all the heritage sites without rushing. MP tourism has some lovely tents here 

📌 SAVE this post for your next offbeat Madhya Pradesh travel itinerary!

#Amarkantak #MadhyaPradeshTourism #IncredibleIndia #TempleArchitecture #TempleStories".

lakshmisharath on August 25, 2026: "This towering ladder isn’t for climbing—it’s the center of ancient exorcism rituals in Chaugan, MP.🤫👇

Deep in Madhya Pradesh lies Chaugan, a place that doesn’t look like your typical tourist destination. 

Known to locals as “The Exorcist Village,” this community lives at the crossroads of intense faith, ancient folklore, and unexplained phenomena.The towering iron ladder you see here isn’t just structure—it’s the center of spiritual rituals where centuries-old traditions are used to ward off dark energies and heal the possessed. In a land built on oral history and deep-rooted beliefs, the thin line between reality and the supernatural completely vanishes.If you are a travel filmmaker, writer, or dark-tourism enthusiast looking to document India’s untold cultural landscapes, this village offers a profound look into rural traditions.

Tips & Recommendations for Visiting Chaugan, MP:📍 

How to get there: Located in the Mandla district of Madhya Pradesh. It is best reached by hiring a local taxi from Jabalpur (the nearest major airport/railway hub).

🤝 Respect local customs: This is a living village with sensitive spiritual practices. Always ask permission before filming people, shrines, or rituals.

💡 Go with a local guide: The folklore here is nuanced. Having a local translator ensures you understand the history accurately without disrespecting the community.

🗓️ Best time to observe: Cultural researchers find festive periods or specific village gathering days offer the deepest look into their traditional practices.

Have you ever visited a place that completely challenged what you believe? Drop your thoughts below. 👇

IndiaOneStoryAtATime #Chaugan #ExorcistVillage #DarkTourismIndia #MadhyaPradeshTourism".

lakshmisharath on August 15, 2026: "INDIA, ONE STORY AT A TIME | 

Episode 1: Meenakshi Amma ⚔️Meeting Padma Shri Meenakshi Amma, the legendary 84-year-old female guru of Kalaripayattu, was a masterclass in local Indian culture and deep historical legacy.

This Independence Day, I am incredibly proud to launch a brand-new series: 

India, One Story at a Time 🇮🇳✨. This project is a celebration of unsung heroes, centuries-old traditions, ancient crafts, beliefs, and living heritage from every corner of our country. Because India is vast, multi-layered, and it is never just one story!There is no better way to begin than in this sacred arena. 

Did you know that during British colonial rule, this ancient Indian martial art was banned and heavily suppressed? To survive, practitioners had to protect and transmit this fierce warrior tradition secretly from Guru to Shishya in hidden underground spaces. Today, this beautiful heritage—widely considered the mother of all martial arts that predates Shaolin Kung Fu—is echoing through a brave new generation of young, confident girls training with swords and shields.

📍 WHERE TO SEE KALARIPAYATTU IN KERALA:

Location: Kadathanadan Kalari Sangham, Vadakara, North Malabar, Kerala.What you see: Hyper-fast sparring with traditional metal swords, shields, and the deadly flexible urumi blade.

Travel tip: Incorporate an authentic Kalari visit into your offbeat Kerala itinerary to truly experience intentional slow travel.

👇 WHAT UNTOLD STORY SHOULD I COVER NEXT?Let me know your destination or heritage suggestions in the comments below! 💬

🔔 If you love discovering hidden history, ancient temples, and raw cultural storytelling across India, hit FOLLOW @lakshmisharath so you don't miss Episode 2 next week! 

🗺️#Kalaripayattu #MeenakshiAmma #IncredibleIndia #KeralaTourism".

lakshmisharath on October 6, 2026: "I went to Gangotri with prayers and stood before Ganga Maa at Gangotri Dham, grateful to be there at last. But my journey also led me into village homes, local legends and friendships. ❤️

Village Ways invited me to experience Rural Stays Gangotri, an initiative supported by UNDP and implemented with local communities.

In Jhala, I stayed in a cosy little homestay overlooking the river. Over Pahadi meals and late-night conversations, my young hostesses, Jyoti and Khushi, became friends.

In Purali, we stepped into an old wooden house shared by four generations and nearly thirty family members. Chanda Devi’s stories made me linger, while the women showed us their handmade crafts.

With Dhiraj, we followed old pilgrim trails beside the river, wandered through apple orchards and heard legends of village temples.

And then came Selku—a centuries-old local festival. Dressed in Garhwali attire, I danced with the women and watched the Pashwa enter a trance.

Somewhere along the way, the little Pahadi girl within me came alive. I left a piece of my heart in these villages, with the people who had made me feel at home.

People make places.

Swipe through the journey.  Full travelogue on lakshmisharath.com

#Gangotri #Uttarakhand #RuralTourism #Selku #indiaonestoryatatime 

Would you add a village stay and experience on your next trip ?".

lakshmisharath on September 28, 2026: "Jaipur in 24 Hours: A World Tourism Day Special

“If I weren’t in politics, my alternative career would have been travel blogging,” said Honourable Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister and Tourism Minister Diya Kumari ji.

That line set the tone for a day packed with the Rajasthan Creators Conclave, meeting Diya Kumari ji, conversations with fellow creators, a panel with industry leaders on The Future of Tourism: Building the Next Tourism Growth Engine, a lovely stay at ITC Rajputana—and a quick safari at Jhalana, where we were lucky to spot leopards.

As someone who began travel blogging in 2005, her words made me smile. Storytelling has shaped the way I have travelled, understood places and connected with people for over two decades.

At the conclave, we spoke about tourism, technology, AI and content. My own conversation kept returning to local cultures, communities and experiences—and how they can become powerful drivers of tourism.

From the energy of the conclave to the stillness of Jhalana, Jaipur packed many different experiences into a single day.

Travel storytelling can make the overlooked visible. And sometimes, all it takes is one story to make us look at a familiar destination differently.

#WorldTourismDay #Jaipur #RajasthanCreatorsConclave #RajasthanTourism #travelstorytelling".

lakshmisharath on September 21, 2026: "Devprayag is where the Ganga gets her name—at the sacred sangam where the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet and flow onwards as one river. It is also one of Uttarakhand’s five sacred Panch Prayags.

SAVE THIS MINI TRAVEL GUIDE

📍 Places to visit
• Devprayag Sangam and the ghats
• Gangeshwar Mahadev Temple beside the sangam
• Raghunathji Temple, dedicated to Lord Rama
• The bridges and viewpoints overlooking the confluence

🚗 How to reach
Devprayag is around 70–75 km from Rishikesh and takes approximately three hours by road. Shared taxis and buses are also available.

🗓️ Best time to visit
March to May and October to November. Avoid the peak monsoon months, when landslides and road disruptions are possible.

⏳ Time required
Allow two to three hours. Stay overnight if you would like to experience the town and sangam at a slower pace.

🏡 Where to stay
Devprayag has simple guesthouses and homestays. Rishikesh and Srinagar offer more accommodation options.

Save this Devprayag travel guide for your Uttarakhand journey.

India, one story at a time.

#Devprayag #Uttarakhand #Ganga #Indiaonestoryatatime #templesofindia".

lakshmisharath on September 11, 2026: "A hundred years of food, tradition and memories.

Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan in Balepet has been part of Bangalore since 1926. For generations of Bangaloreans, it has been much more than a restaurant—it is nostalgia, a family tradition and almost a rite of passage.

Places like this don’t simply preserve the flavours of a city. They become part of its story.

#UdupiSriKrishnaBhavan #OldBangalore #BangaloreFood #BengaluruHeritage

Have you been to Udupi Shri Krishna Bhavan in Balapet ?".

lakshmisharath on September 3, 2026: "This is Lord Krishna’s office. Across the sea is his home,” my driver said as we entered Dwarka.

The salt of the sea filled the air. Somewhere beneath lies Krishna’s submerged city, believed lost to the sea.

Photos 1–3 | Krishna’s kingdom by the sea

To the people here, Dwarka is not just a temple town. Krishna is worshipped as a king and Dwarkadhish Temple as his palace—Jagat Mandir. Bells chimed, drums rose and red flags fluttered above its towers.

Photos 4–6 | Across the sea to Krishna’s home

The next morning, I followed Krishna across the sea. Colourful boats filled Okha harbour, seagulls circled above us and pilgrims sailed to Bet Dwarka, believed to be his island home. A room inside the temple remembers Krishna’s reunion with Sudama; devotees still receive rice, recalling Sudama’s humble gift.

Photo 7 | The queen who stands apart

Back on the mainland stood Rukmini Temple, separated from Krishna’s temple by the legend of Durvasa’s curse.

Photos 8–9 | A friendship remembered

In Porbandar, Sudama’s home, murals inside Sudama Temple brought their enduring friendship to life.

Photos 10–15 | Krishna’s final journey

Near Somnath, the Krishna trail became quieter. Banganga, Bhalka Tirth and Dehotsarg are associated with his final journey—where a hunter’s arrow is believed to have struck him and where he is said to have left his mortal form.

Beside his footprints at Dehotsarg, I realised that my trail had ended. I had followed Krishna’s footsteps through this mythical land.

Photos 16–17 | Back where the journey began

The sea fell quiet at sunset; the red flag flew above Krishna’s kingdom.

SAVE THIS 4-DAY DWARKA–SOMNATH ITINERARY

Day 1: Dwarkadhish Temple and sunset; stay in Dwarka.
Day 2: Rukmini Temple and Bet Dwarka via Sudarshan Setu; stay in Dwarka.
Day 3: Porbandar (104 km) for Sudama Temple; continue to Somnath (130 km). Stay in Somnath/Veraval.
Day 4: Somnath, Banganga, Bhalka Tirth and Dehotsarg.

TIPS: A cab/self-drive car is easiest. Dwarka has a railway station; airports: Jamnagar and Porbandar. Visit October–February. Janmashtami is crowded. Photography is restricted 

#KrishnaJayanthi #Dwarka #BetDwarka #somnath".

lakshmisharath on August 31, 2026: "August in pictures. 

A new plot twist , small steps , big shifts  and a complete internal reset . 

How was August for you ? 

Ten days went into an Ayurvedic detox—a pause, a reset and a reminder to listen to my body. But even as life slowed down on the outside, a great deal was shifting within. 

There were conversations, projects , gigs , travels , music , books , ideas - writing, planning, creating - a webinar, a concert , a book club quiz . A month dedicated to new directions and several small baby steps towards initiatives  that are still taking shape.

And then there were the moments that did make it to the camera—Yakshagana and temple stories, books and food, friends and furry companions, little journeys and quiet pockets of green.

August was not really a month of finished chapters. It was a month of beginnings—of internal shifts, greater clarity and baby steps towards something new.

Perhaps the most important changes are not always the ones that are captured in photos and videos . 

These are just a few visible fragments of a month that changed much more beneath the surface.

#AugustInPictures #LifeLately #QuietBeginnings #NewBeginnings #august2026".

lakshmisharath on August 17, 2026: "It’s Nag Panchami , Shravan Somvar today 

And am truly blessed to be in this divine temple . 

Hidden in the quiet green lanes of Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, the historic Kaadu Malleshwara Temple comes alive for Nagara Panchami.

If you’ve ever wondered why this day holds such a profound place in our heritage, here is the depth behind the devotion:

🎒 The Traveler’s Guide to Nag Panchami 

An ancient monsoon festival dedicated to worshipping the Naga Devatas (serpent deities).It began as a practical seasonal ritual to pray for safe coexistence as snakes emerged from flooded burrows during the Shravana rains.

The Cosmic Connection: Serpents symbolize heightened consciousness. Lord Shiva wears one to show mastery over fear, and Lord Vishnu rests on the cosmic serpent, Sheshanaga.📜 

Mythology: The 3 Main Legends

Samudra Manthan - The Antidote: When Shiva drank cosmic poison to save the universe, snakes absorbed the stray drops. Devotees offer milk (Abhisheka) to cool them down.

The Taming of Kaliya: It celebrates young Krishna subduing the toxic, multi-hooded serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna River, choosing to tame and spare him to restore ecological balance.

The Great Rescue: It marks the day the sage Astika stopped a catastrophic fire ritual, saving the entire serpent race from extinction.

Stepping into this courtyard today feels like stepping back in time. Pure faith, fresh flowers, and timeless traditions right in the middle of Namma Bengaluru. 

Traveler’s Tip: When you visit, don’t miss the mysterious Dakshina Mukha Nandi Teertha right across the street, where fresh water continuously flows out of Nandi’s mouth from an undiscovered source! Share this guide with a fellow traveller👇

Wishing everyone the divine energy and protection of the Nagas. 

✨#NagPanchami #kadumalleshwaratemple #templesofindia #nagarapanchami🐍 #nammabengaluru❤️".

The Taming of Kaliya: It celebrates young Krishna subduing the toxic, multi-hooded serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna River, choosing to tame and spare him to restore ecological balance.

The Great Rescue: It marks the day the sage Astika stopped a catastrophic fire ritual, saving the entire serpent race from extinction.

Stepping into this courtyard today feels like stepping back in time. Pure faith, fresh flowers, and timeless traditions right in the middle of Namma Bengaluru. 

Traveler’s Tip: When you visit, don’t miss the mysterious Dakshina Mukha Nandi Teertha right across the street, where fresh water continuously flows out of Nandi’s mouth from an undiscovered source! Share this guide with a fellow traveller👇

Wishing everyone the divine energy and protection of the Nagas. 

✨#NagPanchami #kadumalleshwaratemple #templesofindia #nagarapanchami🐍 #nammabengaluru❤️".

Slow journeys. Wandering off the beaten path. Going with the flow. Meeting people, celebrating local cultures, listening to stories and losing myself in ancient temples.

I’ve never really been a bucket-list traveller. I’d rather collect experiences — the unexpected encounters, little detours and stories that stay with you long after the journey is over.

And while I love exploring the world, there’s something about travelling through India that never stops fascinating me. There’s always another story, another place, another experience waiting to be discovered.

50 countries in… but India, always. ❤️

That’s my kinda chic. What’s yours ?

lakshmisharath on August 2, 2026: "Flower Therapy ! 

At KR Flower Market, every bloom has a destination. A temple. A wedding. A festival. A home. What begins here quietly becomes part of countless celebrations across the city.

Come early, breathe in the fragrance of fresh jasmine and marigolds, watch the garland makers at work, and lose yourself in one of Bengaluru’s most colourful morning rituals.

There’s something magical about places that come alive before sunrise. And the best way to experience a city is simply to wander.

#KRFlowerMarket #Bengaluru #BangaloreDiaries #FlowerMarket".
